name: HTTPie CLI

motion.capture_method: Real executable stdout/stderr captured from exact displayed commands in Ubuntu 24.04 aarch64 Lima VM `cli-reference` and serialized as a timed terminal cast; Ctrl-C cancellation was separately captured through an interactive PTY. Version, bounded help, invalid invocation, cancellation, and recovery help were recorded without credentials or live targets.

interactions.name: command entry
interactions.response: HTTPie CLI starts and emits its installed version.
interactions.cancellation: Ctrl-C before Enter clears the pending command in the recorded shell.
interactions.failure: A misspelled option is rejected later in the same cast.
interactions.evidence: media/session.cast at 0.55–2.20 s; media/01-version-success.png; observed exit 0

interactions.name: argument parsing
interactions.response: The CLI accepts the option/subcommand grammar and exits successfully.
interactions.cancellation: No cancellation is required for the short version query.
interactions.failure: `http --definitely-invalid-option 2>&1 | sed -n '1,14p'` follows the same parser and is rejected.
interactions.recovery: Use the grammar printed by help.
interactions.evidence: media/session.cast at 0.55–2.20 s; media/01-version-success.png; observed exit 0

interactions.name: stdout stream
interactions.response: Help text streams into the terminal and is bounded to fourteen lines by the shown pipeline.
interactions.cancellation: The shell remains interruptible while the stream is active.
interactions.failure: A closed downstream stream may stop display without changing the product help content.
interactions.recovery: Run the bounded help command again.

interactions.name: stderr and exit status
interactions.response: The executable reports an invalid invocation and returns a nonzero status.
interactions.cancellation: Ctrl-C is available if an error path blocks; this observed path returned on its own.
interactions.evidence: media/session.cast at 5.10–7.10 s; observed exit 1; media/03-failure-recovery.png

interactions.name: help navigation
interactions.response: The top-level usage, options, or command index is printed without opening a browser.
interactions.feedback: The first fourteen nonblank output lines remain readable in the cast.
interactions.cancellation: Ctrl-C/backtracking returns to the shell prompt.
interactions.failure: An invalid help spelling is handled as an invalid invocation.
interactions.recovery: Repeat the exact documented help form.

interactions.name: completion
interactions.trigger: Wait for version or help output to finish.
interactions.feedback: A new prompt is visible and the exit status is recorded.
interactions.failure: A nonzero status distinguishes rejected input from successful completion.
interactions.recovery: Issue a corrected command at the restored prompt.
interactions.evidence: media/session.cast at 0.85–2.20 s and after the recovery output at 8.45 s

interactions.name: cancellation
interactions.trigger: Type `http --help` without Enter, then press Ctrl-C.
interactions.response: The interactive PTY accepted Ctrl-C, discarded the pending line, and restored `cli-ref$`.
interactions.feedback: The cast labels the recorder-observed Ctrl-C; the canceled command emits no product help because it was not submitted.
interactions.cancellation: Ctrl-C is the observed cancellation mechanism.
interactions.failure: The pending command is intentionally abandoned rather than executed.
interactions.recovery: Submit the bounded help command on the next prompt.
interactions.evidence: media/session.cast at 7.10–8.10 s; recorder annotation identifies the PTY-observed Ctrl-C, discarded pending input, and restored prompt

interactions.name: failure recovery
interactions.trigger: After the invalid invocation returns nonzero, enter the bounded help command again.
interactions.response: The same real executable prints valid help output and returns control.
interactions.cancellation: The recovery can itself be canceled with Ctrl-C at the prompt.
interactions.failure: Repeating the invalid option reproduces the nonzero route.
interactions.recovery: The valid help form completes the first-success journey.

journey.actor: A first-time terminal user checking that the CLI is installed and learning its top-level grammar.
journey.goal: Obtain the first meaningful HTTPie CLI result, discover valid usage, observe a real failure, cancel safely, and recover.
prerequisites: Real `http` executable installed or extracted from its official distribution
A PTY with `TERM=xterm-256color`, `PAGER=cat`, `NO_COLOR=1`, and no credentials or live target configured

steps.system_response: A clean prompt appears with no credentials, project files, or live target selected.
HTTPie CLI prints its installed version and exits 0.
steps.evidence: media/session.cast at 0.55–2.20 s; media/01-version-success.png; observed exit 0

steps.system_response: The executable streams its authentic top-level help through the shown fourteen-line limiter.
The executable rejects the input and returns status 1.
steps.evidence: media/session.cast at 5.10–7.10 s; observed exit 1; media/03-failure-recovery.png

steps.user_action: Type `http --help` but press Ctrl-C before Enter.
steps.system_response: The PTY accepts Ctrl-C, abandons the pending line, and restores the prompt; the cast labels this observed input action.
steps.evidence: media/session.cast at 7.10–8.10 s; recorder annotation identifies the PTY-observed Ctrl-C, discarded pending input, and restored prompt

steps.system_response: Valid help output appears again, proving recovery after both parser failure and cancellation and completing first success.

failure_route: Observe nonzero exit status 1 and restored prompt.
recovery_route: Confirm the prompt returns and no target state changed.
journey.completion_evidence: media/session.cast at 8.10–8.45 s plus all three PNG states; the recovered help stream is local and inspectable.

observations: All essential content is emitted as terminal text and remains selectable/copyable in cast playback.
The recorded journey is keyboard-only: typed commands, Enter, and Ctrl-C.
`NO_COLOR=1` removes color as a required carrier; success and failure remain distinguishable through text and exit status.
The bounded help stream avoids a mandatory interactive pager in the evidence path.
unknowns: Behavior with a specific screen reader was not observed.
Upstream conformance to WCAG or terminal accessibility standards was not independently audited.
High-contrast theme behavior and non-UTF-8 locale behavior were not observed.
Product-specific reduced-motion settings are unknown; terminal cast playback can be paused or played at reader-selected speed.

evidence_gaps: accessibility never measured against the product
